meta.title: Physics Day: Four Short Texts
meta.textType: parts of a note, a caption, a blog post, and instructions

paragraphs: Physics Day: Four Short Texts, posted by Mia. Last Saturday, the Explorers started a short physics course at the science museum. Physics is the science of things that move and fall. Guide Ann was our teacher, and she gave us a lot of paper. After the course, I wrote four short texts. Each text has parts, and I will name them. Do you remember the parts of a note?

First, here is the note from Guide Ann. The note begins with the greeting, "Dear Explorers." The next part gives the details, "The course is on Saturday at ten o'clock in the Space Room." Then the note says, "For further information, please ask Teacher Kim." It ends with the closing, "Thank you, Guide Ann." The details are the most important part of a note like this.

Second, here is the caption of my photo. The photo shows a paper helicopter in the air above Leo's hand. The caption says, "A paper helicopter falls and turns." A caption names the thing in the photo. It can also tell what happens. I took the photo at the right moment, and Leo was very happy. It was not easy, because the helicopter moved fast.

Third, here is my blog post. The title is "Physics Is Not Hard," and the writer is Mia. In the post, I write, "At first, physics looks hard, but it is fun." I also write, "We tried various kinds of paper in a test." The facts come from the test, and the opinion is mine. The post ends with a question, "Do you want to try it?" A blog post has a title, a writer, a middle part, and a last line.

Last, here are the instructions for a paper helicopter. The title says, "How to Make a Paper Helicopter." Step one says, "Cut a long piece of normal paper." Step two says, "Cut the top part in the middle, and make two wings." Step three says, "Drop the helicopter from a high place." Step four says, "Watch it fall and turn." Instructions have steps in order, and each step is short. Leo made six helicopters, and I made five.
Now you know the parts of four short texts. Which part is the easiest to find? Try the experiment at home, and take a photo.
